newsitem.title: DUBAI: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - July 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - July 3.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Qatar said it was going ahead with preparations for a controversial Arab-Israeli economic summit in November, despite pressure from other Arab countries to cancel or postpone it.
- The UAE's ministry of labour and social affairs has started approving part-time and temporary jobs.
- The financial reserves of the six Gulf Arab states declined by around $1 billion in the 12 months to the end of March despite a sharp increase in oil income, an Arab Banking Corp bulletin said.
- The Dubai court of cassation ruled that the amount of blood money for manslaughter was fixed by law at 150,000 dirhams ($41,000) and could not be changed under any circumstances.
- DHL, Tajik Air and Kmart announced they had set up offices in Sharjah Airport's duty free zone.
- Oman Air has introduced flights to Madras and Doha.

- Sharjah International Airport Free Zone said that with 250 new companies starting operations from the zone, it was on course to meet its target of drawing 300 firms by the end of the year. Some 252 companies are now operating from the zone.
- Abu Dhabi re-exports set a new record in May, rising to 77.8 million dirhams from 57.1 million dirhams in the year-ago period, statistics from the customs department said.
- Philippine exports to the UAE in the first three months of the year increased to $29.9 million from $20.7 million in the same period a year ago.
- The UAE's financial reserves rose to $8.72 billion in the year to March, up from $7.97 billion in the corresponding period a year earlier, statistics showed.
